first_frame: A split-screen video showing a man with a robotic eye overlay (top) and the original raw footage (bottom). Text overlay: 'CYBERPUNK INDIA'.
beats: 0-32 s: A montage of 'Cyberpunk India' visuals, split-screen showing AI CGI vs. raw footage.
32-35 s: Talking head intro explaining the tool used (Higgsfield Genjutsu).
35-89 s: Step-by-step tutorial on how to use the tool, intercut with more examples and screen recordings of the app interface.
visual_techniques: Screen recording of software interface (58-62 s, 101-104 s)
B-roll of the creator filming on location (38-42 s)
Fast-paced cuts between tutorial steps and visual examples (45-57 s)
captions: Simple white sans-serif font, 3-6 words per chunk, centered, no highlight colour.
sound: Upbeat, futuristic electronic background music, voiceover narration, sound effects of robotic movements and city ambiance.
recurring_element: The split-screen 'AI CGI vs. RAW' comparison.
why: The video is essentially a long-form tutorial disguised as a short. The hook is visually impressive, but the transition into a 60-second 'how-to' guide causes a significant drop in retention for viewers expecting a quick, entertaining showcase of 'Cyberpunk India'. The pacing slows down too much during the technical explanation.
reusable_faceless: Screen recording with zoom-ins on specific UI elements
Overlaying text on top of raw footage to explain the process
Using a 'step-by-step' structure for complex AI tools
